lawyer:
Monindra Biswas ----- Plaintiffs-Respondents-Petitioners
vs
Khalilur Rahman Chowdhury ----- Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Party
parties:
Md Zakir Hossain with Abdul Jalil, Advocates — For the Petitioners. 

AKM Badrudduza, Advocate — For the Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 22-6-2008 (decree signed on 29-6-2008), passed by the Additional District Judge, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No.141 of 2006, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 26-2-2006 (decree signed on 3-5-2006), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No.85 of 2005, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that Sree Monindra Chandra Biswas and two others had filed Title Suit No.66 of 2003 before the Court of 1st Assistant Judge, Gazipur, against Khalilur Rahman Chowdhury (the principal-defendant) and another i.e. the Sub-Registrar, Gazipur Sadar, Gazipur, being the pro-forma defendant, which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.85 of 2005. The said suit was filed for rectification of a deed No.2347, dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit-1), which the plaintiff has executed in favour of the defendant No.1. In that suit, the plaintiff has prayed that, the deed should be rectified/ amended by deleting PS Plot No.1406, as described in schedule "Kha" to the plaint, on the allegation that, the said deed was executed to convey and transfer title in PS Plot No.1410, as described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint, and that, possession of the said PS Plot No.1410 was handed over to the defendant. Subsequently, the defendant claimed that, he had purchased 0.1750 acres of land from PS Plot No.1406. Thereafter, the plaintiff made a search in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Gazipur on 17-12-2002 and obtained the certified copy of the said deed No.2347, dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit-1) and found that, in the schedule of the said deed, PS Plot Nos.1406 and 1410 have also been written in the schedule to the deed. The further case of the plaintiff is that, PS Plot No.1406 has been inserted fraudulently by the plaintiff in-connivance with the witnesses to the deed and the deed writer. Therefore, the plaintiffs had filed this suit for rectification of the said deed by deleting PS Plot No.1406 from the schedule to the said deed. 

3. The defendant has appeared in the suit by filing written statement, on 15-6-2003, wherein he has claimed that, he has purchased 0.1750 acres of land from PS Plot No. 1406, as was proposed by the plaintiff to be sold to the defendant and he has been given possession of 0.1750 acres of land in that plot. His specific case has been stated in paragraph No. 9 of the written statement. 

4. The plaintiff's side adduced 4 witnesses and proved certain documents, marked as exhibits 1-8 respectively, while the defendant adduced 3 witnesses and proved certain documents, marked as exhibits `Ka' and 'Kha'. 

5. The trial Court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the oral and the documentary evidences, had decreed the suit; vide its judgment and decree dated 26-2-2006 (decree signed on 5-3-2006). 

6. Against the said judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the Defendant preferred Title Appeal No.141 of 2006 before the District Judge, Gazipur, which was heard by the Court of Additional District Judge, Gazipur, who, being the Appellate Court, has passed the impugned judgment and decree, allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide its judgment and decree dated 22-6-2008 (decree signed on 29-6-2008) and remanded the suit to the Trial Court with a direction to dispose of the Title Suit No.85 of 2005 and Title Suit No.419 of 2008(filed by the defendant-appellant) analogously. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the Plaintiffs-Respondents-Petitioners have filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and obtained the present Rule.

8. Learned Advocates Mr Md Zakir Hossain and Mr Abdul Jalil appeared for the petitioners. Mr Md Zakir Hossain, having placed the petition submits that 0.1750 acres of land was sold to the defendants out of PS Plot No. 1410; vide deed No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit-1). He next submits that the appellate court has allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court without at all reversing any finding arrived at by the trial court. He proceeds on that, the plaintiffs have sold 0.1750 acres of land from PS Plot No.1410 and, accordingly, the plaintiffs have handed over the possession of the said land of PS Plot No.1410. The learned Advocate continues that, thereafter the defendant has opened a khatian in his name (Exhibit-3) in respect of PS Plot No.1410, not in respect of RS Plot No.1406. He proceeds on that, the oral evidence as well as the documentary evidence clearly proved the case of the plaintiffs and the trial court, upon framing proper issues, had arrived at correct findings, after assessing all the evidences, and had decreed the suit, but the appellate court, without reversing any finding of the trial court, has most arbitrarily allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and then remanded the Title Suit No.85 of 2005 for analogous hearing of Title Suit No.419 of 208 filed "by the defendant against the plaintiffs about 2(two) years after the disposal of the Title Suit No.85 of 2005. He also submits that, the order for remand was made on the basis of an application filed by the defendant-appellant for analogous hearing of both the Title Suit Nos. 85 of 2005 and 419 of 2008, i.e. not on merit. The learned Advocate next submits that the appellate court has committed error of law in passing the judgment and decree which has resulted in error in the decision, causing serious prejudice to the petitioners. The learned Advocate has referred to a decision reported in 7 BLT (AD) 145 = 4 BLC (AD) 72, between Indrajit Kundu and others vs S Ali, in support of his contention. He lastly submits that, this Rule has merit and the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court are liable to be set-aside. 

9. Learned Advocate Mr AKM Badrudduza appeared for the defendant-appellant-opposite party. He, at the very outset, points out that there is only one schedule in the disputed deed No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit Kha = Exhibit-1 of the defendant). But in the plaint, the plaintiffs have given two different schedules. He next submits that, in the schedule to the disputed deed, both the PS Plots No.1406 and No. 1410 have been specifically mentioned, out of which 0.1750 acres of land was sold to the defendant and possession has been given in 0.1750 acres of land of PS Plot No.1406, since that was intended to be purchased by the defendant-buyer and was sold to him and that, the defendant is in peaceful and continuous possession of the purchased land by erecting boundary wall and other demarcation. He next submits that, in the report of the Advocate Commissioner, both the PS Plot Nos.1406 and 1410 have been marked with green colour as the disputed land, while the Advocate Commissioner has also marked PS Plot No. 1413 in green colour as the disputed property, which is not in the schedule to the disputed deed. He next submits that, the Advocate Commissioner's report is not correct, rather it is misleading, and reliance on the said report by the trial court was not proper. He proceeds on that, the defendant is the bonafide purchaser for value and, in fact, the plaintiffs have no title in PS Plot No. 1410, which was acquired by the Government and the plaintiffs has handed over possession of 0.1740 acres of land from PS Plot No. 1406 and the defendant-purchaser is still possessing the same. He further submits that, there is no consistency between the prayer portion of the plaint and the schedule of the plaint and that, there is no evidence on record to prove any case of fraud as alleged. He next submits that, exhibit-3, which is claimed to be mutation khatian of the defendant, is an unsigned document and the same was not admissible in evidence. Hence, the trial court should not have marked the said khatian as exhibit No. 3 and the trial court should not have relied upon exhibit-3 to arrive at the finding in passing the judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff. As regards the judgment of the appellate court, the learned Advocate submits that, the defendant filed Title Suit No. 419 of 2008 for rectification of the sale deed No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit Kha = Exhibit-1) by deleting PS Plot No. 1410 from the said deed, therefore, in order to avoid a conflicting judgments and having found that the judgment of the trial court was not proper, the appellate court has rightly set-aside the judgment of the trial court and that tantamounts to reversal of the findings of the trial court and, therefore, had sent the suit on remand for fresh trial of Title Suit No. 85 of 2005 along with Title Suit No. 419 of 2008, so that the case and evidences of both the parties can be considered together and a proper judgment can be passed. He also submits that, the appellate court is competent to send the Title Suit 85 of 2005 on remand and in passing the judgment and decree of the trial court; the appellate court has committed no error of law causing any prejudice to the parties. He, therefore, submits that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged. 

10. I have heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the petition and judgment of both the courts below and also other materials on record. 

11. It is not disputed by either of the parties that, the plaintiffs have executed the deed No. No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit-Kha of the defendant = Exhibit 1 of the plaintiffs), whereby the plaintiffs have transferred 0.1750 acres of land. Admittedly, the only dispute between the parties is that, the plaintiffs are claiming that 0.1750 acres of land was sold from PS Plot No. 1410, not from PS Plot No. 1406. The plaintiff's further case is that, the defendant had inserted PS Plot No. 1406 in connivance with the deed writer and with the witnesses of the deed and that they have come to know about the above insertion of PS Plot No.1406 after obtaining certified copy of the No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit-Kha = 1) on 17-12-2002 and, thereafter, they have filed Title Suit No. 66 of 2003, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.85 of 2005. On the contrary, the defendant's case is that, he intended to buy 0.1750 acres of land which he has been possessing since the date of sale and that is lying under PS Plot No. 1406 and that he has been possessing the purchased property within specific demarcated boundary. 

12. I have examined the deed No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit-Kha = Exhibirt-1). I find that there is only one schedule in the said deed and that 0.1750 acres of land was sold from PS plot No. 1410 and PS Plot No. 1406. I also find that the plaintiffs did not deny that the said deed has been executed out of free will and it is duly attested, as per law. I also find that, it has been written, at the end of the said deed that, 
“এতদ্বার্থে স্বেচ্ছায় স্বজ্ঞানে সুস্থশরীরে অন্যের বিনা প্ররোচনায় অত্র সাফ কবলা দলিল লিখাইয়া টাইপ করাইয়া পড়িয়া ও পড়াইয়া এবং ইহার মর্ম অবগত অত্র সাফ কবলা দলিল আমরা সহি সম্পাদন করিয়া দিলাম ।”Hence, the genuineness of the said deed is apparent and the plaintiff's evidence, if any, to prove that the Plot No. 1406 was subsequently inserted, by fraud or connivance, should be inadmissible and be excluded, as per provisions of section 91 of the Evidence Act, 1872. 

13. The court below must note that, the only dispute in this case is in which of these 2(two) PS Plots, namely, PS Plot No. 1406 and PS Plot No. 1410, this 0.1750 acres of land was intended to be sold. 

14. However, the appellate court has duty to decide the case on merit, as required by rule 24 of Order 41, of the Code of Civil Procedure, if it finds that the evidence produced before it are sufficient to enable it to pronounce the judgment, otherwise the appellate court can remand the case either under rule 23 or as per provisions laid down in rule 25 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

15. In the instant case the appellate court has remanded the case on the basis of an application for analogous hearing of a disposed of suit No. 85 of 2005 (which was pending as an appeal) for analogous hearing with Title Suit No. 419 of 2008, pending before the court of Assistant Judge, having stated as reason that, unless these 2(two) matters are heard analogously then there is likelihood of conflict of judgment. 

16. In my considered opinion, the appellate court has ample power to send the case on remand, either under rule 23 or rule 25 or Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But, in the instant case the impugned judgment and decree has not been passed as per rule 23 or rule 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure. On the other hand the appellate court cannot set-aside the judgment of the trial court without reversing the findings of the trial court, which require the appellate court judgment and order on merit. 

17. Hence, I am constrained to hold that, the appellate court has failed to exercise its power as per provisions of rule 24 or, in the case of remand, as per provisions laid down in rule 23 or 25 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

18. The judgment of the appellate court has not been passed either on merit or on preliminary issue. 

19. As such, and in view of the above, I hold that, the appellate court has committed error of law in passing the impugned judgment, resulted in error in its decision and that has caused prejudice to the plaintiffs-respondents. 

20. I have also perused the judgment reported in 7 BLT (AD) 145 = 4 BLC (AD) 72 between Indrajit Kundu and others vs S Ali. In that case, both the courts below have decided the case on merit on the basis of evidence on record and it was held by the Appellate Division that, the High Court Division was not justified in law in sending back the case on remand to the trial court, in that situation, for holding trial afresh. The judgment of the Appellate Division is binding on the High Court Division and it has laid down a clear law, but this judgment is not applicable in this matter, because in the instant case, the appellate court has not decided the appeal on merit. Rather, it has disposed of the appeal on the basis of an application filed by the defendant-appellant for analogous hearing of Title Suit Nos. 85 of 2005 and 419 of 2008. As such, in this case before me, the appellate court has not arrived at its own findings, as the last court of fact. 

21. Therefore, the impugned judgment and order should be set-aside and the appellate court should be directed to re-hear the appeal afresh and to pronounce a proper judgment or order upon hearing the parties, as per provisions of law as stated above. Hence, I am not inclined to make any comment about the merit of the case, except that, the evidence, if any, adduced by the plaintiffs to rebut the contents of Exhibit 1 = Exhibit Kha as well as the evidence adduced to prove that the PS Plot No. 1406 has been subsequently inserted in Exhibit 1 = Exhibit Kha, should be inadmissible and be excluded as per provisions of section 91 of the Evidence Act, 1872. Here, it has to be noted that, the defendant-buyer is entitled to get possession of 0.1750 acres of land, from either or both of these two PS Plots No. 1406 and 1410, as per the admitted sale deed (Exhibit 1 = Exhibit 'Kha') therefore, the main point for determination, in this case, is to ascertain from which, out of these two plots, 0.1750 acres of lands was intended to be sold. 

22. Besides, the court below shall keep in mind that, this is a suit for rectification of a deed, as per provisions of section 31 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, not a suit for declaration of title under section 42 of the said Act. The distinction is clear as the issues involved are distinct too. 

23. The appellate court shall, in deciding this appeal, frame amongst other, the following points (issues) for determination, namely, (I) In which out of these 3(three) Plots namely, PS Plot No. 1406 and PS Plot No. 1410, the defendant has been given possession of 0.1750 acres of land. (II) Whether the defendant-appellant-purchaser is in peaceful and uninterrupted possession of 0.1750 acres of land in PS Plot No. 1406 and (III) Which, out of these two PS Plots, 0.1750 acres of land was intended to be sold to the purchaser and then shall pronounce the judgment accordingly, if it considers that the evidence is adequate for deciding the case, otherwise it may remand the case as per rule 23 or rule 25 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or may, in an appropriate case, take additional evidence as per law.

24. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and decree dated 22-6-2008 (decree signed on 29-6-2018) in Title Appeal No. 141 of 2006, passed by the Court of Additional District Judge, Gazipur, is hereby set-aside and the case is remanded back to the appellate court for hearing afresh, in the light of the observations made above. 

25. The Rule is disposed of accordingly. 

26. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated. 

27. Parties will bear their respective costs. Let a copy of this judgment along with LCR be sent to the concerned Courts at once. 

End.
